1	/**
2	 * Snapshot the committed replay fixtures under `public/fixtures/` from a running feed.
3	 *
4	 * Replay mode shows recorded reality, never invented data: the roster is the
5	 * feed's own `GET /roster`, the runs are committed records the feed discovers
6	 * under `data/code-safety/` and `data/proving-ground/`, the event streams are
7	 * their session logs folded by the feed, and each review is the feed's
8	 * `GET /safety/:id` for the record. Point the feed at the repository (the
9	 * default `pnpm run feed`), then run `pnpm --dir apps/command-deck fixtures`.
10	 *
11	 * Only committed record ids are eligible: a live `.code-safety/<id>` run is
12	 * refused, because its session logs are not redacted before they are recorded.
13	 */
14	import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
15	import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path'
16	import type { Roster, Run, RunEvent, SafetyReview } from '../deck/contract.ts'
17	
18	const here = dirname(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname)
19	const fixtures = resolve(here, '..', 'public', 'fixtures')
20	
21	/** The feed to snapshot from; `FEED_URL` overrides the default local feed. */
22	const FEED = (process.env['FEED_URL'] ?? 'http://localhost:4711').replace(/\/+$/, '')
23	
24	/**
25	 * The records the replay carries: the newest NodeGoat review, the Java review,
26	 * one tier-5 fleet, one paired experiment, one program. Every id names a
27	 * committed record directory; the deck opens on the first code-safety run.
28	 */
29	const RUN_IDS = [
30	  '2026-09-19-nodegoat-2',
31	  '2026-09-19-dvja',
32	  '2026-09-19-bench-h3-baseline-sonnet-t5',
33	  '2026-09-19-bench-e7-attempts-5-t5-2',
34	  '2026-09-19-csv-tools-program',
35	] as const
36	
37	/** How long a stream may stay silent before its replay is considered complete. */
38	const STREAM_IDLE_MS = 2_500
39	
40	/**
41	 * Fetch one JSON payload from the feed.
42	 * @param path - Path starting with `/`.
43	 * @returns The parsed payload.
44	 */
45	async function readJson<T>(path: string): Promise<T> {
46	  const response = await fetch(`${FEED}${path}`)
47	  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path} answered ${response.status}`)
48	  return await response.json() as T
49	}
50	
51	/**
52	 * Read one run's Server-Sent Events replay until the stream goes idle.
53	 *
54	 * The feed replays history and then keeps the connection open, polling the
55	 * session files for appended lines, so a completed run's replay is the frames
56	 * that arrive before the first idle gap.
57	 * @param runId - The run to read.
58	 * @returns Every replayed event, in arrival order.
59	 */
60	async function readEvents(runId: string): Promise<RunEvent[]> {
61	  const controller = new AbortController()
62	  const response = await fetch(`${FEED}/runs/${encodeURIComponent(runId)}/events`, { signal: controller.signal })
63	  if (!response.ok || response.body === null) throw new Error(`/runs/${runId}/events answered ${response.status}`)
64	  const reader = response.body.getReader()
65	  const decoder = new TextDecoder()
66	  const events: RunEvent[] = []
67	  let buffer = ''
68	  let idle: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
69	  const armIdle = (): void => {
70	    if (idle !== undefined) clearTimeout(idle)
71	    idle = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), STREAM_IDLE_MS)
72	  }
73	  armIdle()
74	  try {
75	    for (;;) {
76	      const { value, done } = await reader.read()
77	      if (done) break
78	      armIdle()
79	      buffer += decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })
80	      const frames = buffer.split('\n\n')
81	      buffer = frames.pop() ?? ''
82	      for (const frame of frames) {
83	        const data = frame.split('\n').find(line => line.startsWith('data:'))
84	        if (data !== undefined) events.push(JSON.parse(data.slice(5).trim()) as RunEvent)
85	      }
86	    }
87	  } catch (error) {
88	    // The idle timer aborts the request once the replay has caught up; any other failure is reported.
89	    if (!(error instanceof Error && error.name === 'AbortError')) throw error
90	  } finally {
91	    if (idle !== undefined) clearTimeout(idle)
92	  }
93	  return events
94	}
95	
96	/**
97	 * Write one fixture as two-space JSON with a trailing newline.
98	 * @param relative - Path under `public/fixtures/`.
99	 * @param value - The payload.
100	 */
101	function writeJson(relative: string, value: unknown): void {
102	  const path = resolve(fixtures, relative)
103	  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true })
104	  writeFileSync(path, `${JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)}\n`)
105	}
106	
107	const roster = await readJson<Roster>('/roster')
108	const listed = await readJson<Run[]>('/runs')
109	const runs = RUN_IDS.map((id) => {
110	  const run = listed.find(entry => entry.id === id)
111	  if (run === undefined) throw new Error(`the feed lists no run "${id}"; record it under data/ first`)
112	  if (!run.path.startsWith('data/')) throw new Error(`"${id}" is a live run at ${run.path}, not a committed record; refusing to snapshot it`)
113	  return run
114	})
115	
116	rmSync(resolve(fixtures, 'events'), { recursive: true, force: true })
117	rmSync(resolve(fixtures, 'safety'), { recursive: true, force: true })
118	writeJson('roster.json', roster)
119	writeJson('runs.json', runs)
120	console.log(`roster: ${roster.agents.length} agents, ${roster.edges.length} edges; runs: ${runs.length}`)
121	
122	for (const run of runs) {
123	  const events = await readEvents(run.id)
124	  const path = resolve(fixtures, 'events', `${run.id}.jsonl`)
125	  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true })
126	  writeFileSync(path, events.map(event => JSON.stringify(event)).join('\n') + (events.length > 0 ? '\n' : ''))
127	  console.log(`${run.id}: ${events.length} events`)
128	  if (run.kind === 'code-safety') {
129	    const review = await readJson<SafetyReview>(`/safety/${encodeURIComponent(run.id)}`)
130	    writeJson(`safety/${run.id}.json`, review)
131	    console.log(`${run.id}: ${review.target.files.length} files, ${review.findings.length} findings, verified ${review.certificate.verified}`)
132	  }
133	}
134	// The comparisons are committed static records, not feed paths, so they are
135	// copied straight from `data/code-safety/comparisons/` rather than fetched.
136	// Each one is keyed by the target slug the deck derives from a review's name.
137	const comparisonsRoot = resolve(here, '..', '..', '..', 'data', 'code-safety', 'comparisons')
138	const COMPARISON_SLUGS = ['nodegoat', 'dvja']
139	rmSync(resolve(fixtures, 'comparison'), { recursive: true, force: true })
140	for (const dir of existsSync(comparisonsRoot) ? readdirSync(comparisonsRoot) : []) {
141	  const file = resolve(comparisonsRoot, dir, 'comparison.json')
142	  if (!existsSync(file)) continue
143	  const comparison = JSON.parse(readFileSync(file, 'utf8')) as { target: string }
144	  const slug = COMPARISON_SLUGS.find(candidate => comparison.target.toLowerCase().includes(candidate))
145	  if (slug === undefined) continue
146	  writeJson(`comparison/${slug}.json`, comparison)
147	  console.log(`comparison ${slug}: from ${dir}`)
148	}
149	
150	console.log(`fixtures: ${readdirSync(fixtures).join(', ')}`)
151

1	/**
2	 * The feed contract the Command Deck reads.
3	 *
4	 * These types mirror the HTTP surface documented in `README.md`; the committed
5	 * fixtures under `fixtures/` satisfy the same types, so replay and live mode
6	 * render through one code path.
7	 */
8	
9	/** Lifecycle of one agent definition inside the enterprise roster. */
10	export type AgentStatus = 'defined' | 'active' | 'certified' | 'failed'
11	
12	/** Relationship kinds between two agents in the roster graph. */
13	export type EdgeKind = 'delegates' | 'verifies' | 'judges' | 'merges' | 'reads' | 'reports'
14	
15	/** Event kinds carried by a run's Server-Sent Events stream. */
16	export type EventKind
17	  = 'step' | 'tool' | 'delegation' | 'directive' | 'certificate' | 'finding' | 'merge' | 'refusal'
18	
19	/** Severity ladder shared by findings, events, and the certificate counts. */
20	export type Severity = 'critical' | 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' | 'info'
21	
22	/**
23	 * How far the department traced a finding: `confirmed` read the source, the
24	 * sink and the path between them, `likely` a dangerous sink with a plausible
25	 * source, `possible` the pattern without established reachability.
26	 */
27	export type Confidence = 'confirmed' | 'likely' | 'possible'
28	
29	/** Run categories the deck can subscribe to. */
30	export type RunKind = 'program' | 'fleet' | 'experiment' | 'code-safety'
31	
32	/** The model route an agent is bound to. */
33	export interface AgentRoute {
34	  provider: string
35	  model: string
36	}
37	
38	/** One defined agent in the enterprise. */
39	export interface Agent {
40	  id: string
41	  name: string
42	  role: string
43	  division: string
44	  department?: string
45	  route: AgentRoute
46	  preset: string
47	  skills: string[]
48	  tools: string[]
49	  source: string
50	  status: AgentStatus
51	}
52	
53	/** A named cluster of agents; `purpose` is the one-line charter shown in 3D. */
54	export interface Division {
55	  id: string
56	  name: string
57	  purpose: string
58	}
59	
60	/** A directed relationship between two agents. */
61	export interface RosterEdge {
62	  from: string
63	  to: string
64	  kind: EdgeKind
65	}
66	
67	/** `GET /roster` payload. */
68	export interface Roster {
69	  generatedAt: string
70	  counts: { defined: number; active: number }
71	  divisions: Division[]
72	  agents: Agent[]
73	  edges: RosterEdge[]
74	}
75	
76	/** One entry of `GET /runs`. */
77	export interface Run {
78	  id: string
79	  kind: RunKind
80	  name: string
81	  startedAt: string
82	  endedAt?: string
83	  status: string
84	  path: string
85	}
86	
87	/** One `data:` frame of `GET /runs/:id/events`. */
88	export interface RunEvent {
89	  /** When the frame was logged, in epoch milliseconds. */
90	  ts: number
91	  /** Position inside the frame's own session, counted from one; unique only together with `sessionId`. */
92	  seq: number
93	  agentId: string
94	  sessionId: string
95	  kind: EventKind
96	  label: string
97	  detail?: string
98	  severity?: Severity
99	  file?: string
100	  line?: number
101	}
102	
103	/** One file of the reviewed target repository. */
104	export interface TargetFile {
105	  path: string
106	  bytes: number
107	  language: string
108	}
109	
110	/** The repository under code-safety review. */
111	export interface SafetyTarget {
112	  name: string
113	  path: string
114	  files: TargetFile[]
115	  languages: Record<string, number>
116	}
117	
118	/** A code-safety department's roll-up for one review. */
119	export interface SafetyDepartment {
120	  id: string
121	  name: string
122	  status: string
123	  certified: boolean
124	  findings: number
125	}
126	
127	/** One code-safety finding placed on the target's code. */
128	export interface Finding {
129	  id: string
130	  cwe: string
131	  owasp: string
132	  severity: Severity
133	  confidence: Confidence
134	  title: string
135	  file: string
136	  line: number
137	  snippet: string
138	  evidence: string
139	  impact: string
140	  fix: string
141	  /** Sources the department cited, as the review wrote them. */
142	  references?: string[]
143	}
144	
145	/** The verifier's certificate over a completed review. */
146	export interface SafetyCertificate {
147	  verified: boolean
148	  verifier: string
149	  checkedAt: string
150	  counts: Record<Severity, number>
151	  unverified: string[]
152	}
153	
154	/** `GET /safety/:id` payload. */
155	export interface SafetyReview {
156	  target: SafetyTarget
157	  departments: SafetyDepartment[]
158	  findings: Finding[]
159	  certificate: SafetyCertificate
160	  report: { markdown: string }
161	}
162	
163	/** One approach's score in a target's comparison, as `assemble-comparison.mjs` records it. */
164	export interface ComparisonTier {
165	  id: string
166	  name: string
167	  kind: string
168	  found: number
169	  recall: number
170	  findings: number
171	  onKnown: number
172	  verified: boolean
173	  wall: string
174	  cost: string
175	  detail: string
176	}
177	
178	/** One known issue and which approaches caught it. */
179	export interface ComparisonRow {
180	  id: string
181	  category: string
182	  semgrep: boolean
183	  singleModel: boolean
184	  enterprise: boolean
185	}
186	
187	/**
188	 * One target reviewed three ways and scored against one ground truth, the
189	 * `comparison.json` a committed record carries. It is a static artifact, the
190	 * same in live and replay, so the deck reads it from the committed fixtures in
191	 * both modes rather than from the feed.
192	 */
193	export interface Comparison {
194	  target: string
195	  revision: string
196	  knownIssues: number
197	  date: string
198	  note: string
199	  tiers: ComparisonTier[]
200	  matrix: ComparisonRow[]
201	  bothModelsMiss: string[]
202	  singleModelOnly: string[]
203	  enterpriseOnly: string[]
204	  iterations: ComparisonIteration[]
205	}
206	
207	/**
208	 * One improvement-loop iteration run against the enterprise baseline: the change
209	 * it tested and the decision taken are authored in the record's `iterations.json`;
210	 * the recall, the issues gained and lost against the baseline, and the targets it
211	 * caught are scored from the iteration's own record.
212	 */
213	export interface ComparisonIteration {
214	  id: string
215	  ran: string
216	  record: string
217	  baseline: string
218	  mechanism: string
219	  change: string
220	  targets: string[]
221	  decision: string
222	  reading: string
223	  found: number
224	  recall: number
225	  findings: number
226	  onKnown: number
227	  verified: boolean
228	  wall: string
229	  gained: string[]
230	  lost: string[]
231	  targetsCaught: string[]
232	}
233	
234	/** Severity order used for sorting and for the legend, worst first. */
235	export const SEVERITY_ORDER: readonly Severity[] = ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'info']
236

1	/**
2	 * The deck's HTTP client for the feed, and the replay fallback.
3	 *
4	 * One `FeedSource` drives every read. When the configured feed does not
5	 * answer, `resolveFeed` selects the committed fixtures under `public/fixtures`,
6	 * static files holding the payloads the feed's paths return — so nothing
7	 * downstream knows which it is reading, beyond the `mode` the status bar
8	 * shows. Replay needs no server, which is what lets the deck ship as a static
9	 * export.
10	 */
11	
12	import type { Comparison, Roster, Run, SafetyReview } from './contract.ts'
13	
14	/** Whether the deck is reading a live feed or the committed fixtures. */
15	type FeedMode = 'live' | 'replay'
16	
17	/** Where the deck reads from, and how it got there. */
18	export interface FeedSource {
19	  mode: FeedMode
20	  /** Base URL every path is appended to, without a trailing slash. */
21	  base: string
22	  /** The configured feed URL, shown in the status bar in both modes. */
23	  configured: string
24	  /** Why the deck fell back, shown in the status bar in replay mode. */
25	  reason?: string
26	}
27	
28	/**
29	 * The path prefix the deck is served under: empty unless the build set
30	 * `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH`, as the GitHub Pages export does because a
31	 * repository site lives at `/<repository>`. Public files are reached through it.
32	 */
33	const BASE_PATH = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH ?? ''
34	
35	/** Base URL of the committed fixtures, static files that mirror the feed's paths. */
36	const FIXTURE_BASE = `${BASE_PATH}/fixtures`
37	
38	/** Query parameter naming the feed for one browser tab: `?feed=https://feed.example`. */
39	const FEED_PARAM = 'feed'
40	
41	/** Where the tab remembers a feed named by {@link FEED_PARAM}, so client navigation and a reload keep it. */
42	const FEED_STORAGE_KEY = 'dsh-deck-feed'
43	
44	/**
45	 * The feed named on the page URL, if any, or the one this tab was given
46	 * earlier. A hosted deck follows any feed the viewer's browser can reach this
47	 * way, without a rebuild; the build's `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL` stays the default.
48	 * @returns The feed URL, or `undefined` outside a browser and when none was named.
49	 */
50	function feedOverride(): string | undefined {
51	  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return undefined
52	  const named = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get(FEED_PARAM)
53	  try {
54	    if (named !== null && named !== '') {
55	      window.sessionStorage.setItem(FEED_STORAGE_KEY, named)
56	      return named
57	    }
58	    return window.sessionStorage.getItem(FEED_STORAGE_KEY) ?? undefined
59	  } catch {
60	    // Storage can be unavailable (a private window, blocked site data); the query alone still names the feed for this load.
61	    return named ?? undefined
62	  }
63	}
64	
65	/** The feed named for this tab, else the configured feed URL, else the documented default. */
66	function feedUrl(): string {
67	  const configured = feedOverride() ?? process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_FEED_URL
68	  return (configured === undefined || configured === '' ? 'http://localhost:4711' : configured)
69	    .replace(/\/+$/, '')
70	}
71	
72	/**
73	 * How long the deck waits for the live feed before falling back to fixtures.
74	 * A cold feed answers `GET /roster` in about 1.5 s on a tree with fifty runs,
75	 * so the probe allows several times that.
76	 */
77	const PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000
78	
79	/**
80	 * Decide where this session reads from.
81	 *
82	 * The probe is one `GET /roster` against the configured feed. Any failure —
83	 * refused connection, timeout, non-2xx, blocked cross-origin request — selects
84	 * replay, because a demo must never show an empty deck.
85	 * @returns The selected source, with the fallback reason when it fell back.
86	 */
87	export async function resolveFeed(): Promise<FeedSource> {
88	  const configured = feedUrl()
89	  try {
90	    const response = await fetch(`${configured}/roster`, {
91	      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS),
92	      cache: 'no-store',
93	    })
94	    if (!response.ok) {
95	      return { mode: 'replay', base: FIXTURE_BASE, configured, reason: `feed answered ${response.status}` }
96	    }
97	    return { mode: 'live', base: configured, configured }
98	  } catch (error) {
99	    return { mode: 'replay', base: FIXTURE_BASE, configured, reason: probeFailure(error) }
100	  }
101	}
102	
103	/**
104	 * Say why the probe failed in terms a viewer can act on.
105	 *
106	 * `fetch` reports a refused connection, a blocked cross-origin request and a
107	 * DNS failure all as one opaque `TypeError`, so the deck states the one thing
108	 * it does know — that nothing answered — instead of repeating the browser's
109	 * wording.
110	 * @param error - Whatever the probe threw.
111	 * @returns A short reason for the status bar.
112	 */
113	function probeFailure(error: unknown): string {
114	  if (error instanceof DOMException && error.name === 'TimeoutError') return 'feed timed out'
115	  if (error instanceof Error && error.name === 'AbortError') return 'feed timed out'
116	  return 'feed unreachable'
117	}
118	
119	/**
120	 * The URL of one feed path on the selected source: the path itself on a live
121	 * feed, the committed JSON file that mirrors it in replay.
122	 * @param source - Source from {@link resolveFeed}.
123	 * @param path - Feed path starting with `/`.
124	 * @returns The URL to fetch.
125	 */
126	function urlOf(source: FeedSource, path: string): string {
127	  return source.mode === 'live' ? `${source.base}${path}` : `${source.base}${path}.json`
128	}
129	
130	/**
131	 * Read one JSON payload from the selected source.
132	 * @param source - Source from {@link resolveFeed}.
133	 * @param path - Feed path starting with `/`.
134	 * @returns The parsed payload.
135	 */
136	async function readJson<T>(source: FeedSource, path: string): Promise<T> {
137	  const response = await fetch(urlOf(source, path), { cache: 'no-store' })
138	  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${path} answered ${response.status}`)
139	  return await response.json() as T
140	}
141	
142	/**
143	 * `GET /roster`.
144	 * @param source - Source from {@link resolveFeed}.
145	 * @returns The enterprise roster.
146	 */
147	export function getRoster(source: FeedSource): Promise<Roster> {
148	  return readJson<Roster>(source, '/roster')
149	}
150	
151	/**
152	 * `GET /runs`.
153	 * @param source - Source from {@link resolveFeed}.
154	 * @returns Every run the feed knows about.
155	 */
156	export function getRuns(source: FeedSource): Promise<Run[]> {
157	  return readJson<Run[]>(source, '/runs')
158	}
159	
160	/**
161	 * `GET /safety/:id`.
162	 * @param source - Source from {@link resolveFeed}.
163	 * @param id - Run id of the review.
164	 * @returns The review, its findings, and its certificate.
165	 */
166	export function getSafety(source: FeedSource, id: string): Promise<SafetyReview> {
167	  return readJson<SafetyReview>(source, `/safety/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`)
168	}
169	
170	/**
171	 * The committed comparison for one target slug, or `undefined` when none is
172	 * bundled. A comparison is a static record (a target reviewed three ways and
173	 * scored against one ground truth), identical in live and replay, so it is
174	 * always read from the committed fixtures under `public/fixtures/comparison`,
175	 * never from the feed.
176	 * @param slug - The target slug, e.g. `nodegoat`.
177	 * @returns The comparison, or `undefined` when the target has none.
178	 */
179	export async function getComparison(slug: string): Promise<Comparison | undefined> {
180	  try {
181	    const response = await fetch(`${FIXTURE_BASE}/comparison/${encodeURIComponent(slug)}.json`, { cache: 'no-store' })
182	    if (!response.ok) return undefined
183	    return await response.json() as Comparison
184	  } catch {
185	    // No comparison bundled for this target, or the fetch failed: the deck hides the tab.
186	    return undefined
187	  }
188	}
189	
190	/**
191	 * The comparison target slug a review's name maps to, or `undefined` when the
192	 * target has no bundled comparison. The review's name is its run id, which
193	 * carries the target name; a slug matches when the id contains it.
194	 * @param reviewName - The review's `target.name`, the run id.
195	 * @returns The slug to pass to {@link getComparison}, or `undefined`.
196	 */
197	export function comparisonSlugFor(reviewName: string): string | undefined {
198	  const lower = reviewName.toLowerCase()
199	  return ['nodegoat', 'dvja'].find(slug => lower.includes(slug))
200	}
201	
202	/**
203	 * The URL of one run's event stream: the feed's Server-Sent Events endpoint on
204	 * a live feed, the committed JSON Lines recording in replay.
205	 * @param source - Source from {@link resolveFeed}.
206	 * @param runId - The run to follow.
207	 * @returns The URL the stream client opens.
208	 */
209	export function eventsUrl(source: FeedSource, runId: string): string {
210	  const id = encodeURIComponent(runId)
211	  return source.mode === 'live' ? `${source.base}/runs/${id}/events` : `${source.base}/events/${id}.jsonl`
212	}
213	
214	/**
215	 * `POST /safety` — start a review of one target.
216	 *
217	 * Replay cannot start a review, so it reopens the recorded one instead; the
218	 * form says so in replay mode, and the deck then follows that run exactly as
219	 * it would follow a freshly started live one.
220	 * @param source - Source from {@link resolveFeed}.
221	 * @param target - Path of the repository to review.
222	 * @param model - Optional model override for the review's agents.
223	 * @returns The started run's id.
224	 */
225	export async function startSafety(source: FeedSource, target: string, model?: string): Promise<string> {
226	  if (source.mode === 'replay') {
227	    const recorded = (await getRuns(source)).find(run => run.kind === 'code-safety')
228	    if (recorded === undefined) throw new Error('no recorded code-safety run to reopen')
229	    return recorded.id
230	  }
231	  const response = await fetch(`${source.base}/safety`, {
232	    method: 'POST',
233	    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
234	    body: JSON.stringify(model === undefined || model === '' ? { target } : { target, model }),
235	  })
236	  if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`POST /safety answered ${response.status}`)
237	  const body = await response.json() as { id?: unknown }
238	  if (typeof body.id !== 'string') throw new Error('POST /safety returned no run id')
239	  return body.id
240	}

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * The run event stream client.
3	 *
4	 * `GET /runs/:id/events` replays history and then stays open, so a reconnect
5	 * receives frames the deck already holds. Every frame carries a `seq` that
6	 * counts from one inside its own session, so deduplication keys on the pair of
7	 * `sessionId` and `seq`: the caller's `onEvent` sees each pair exactly once for
8	 * the life of the subscription, across any number of reconnections. Keying on
9	 * `seq` alone kept 404 of the 1,079 frames of a seven-session review.
10	 *
11	 * In replay the same subscription reads a committed recording once and paces
12	 * it the way the feed would have streamed it, so the views cannot tell the two
13	 * apart; a recording is read once, so it is not deduplicated.
14	 */
15	
16	import type { RunEvent } from './contract.ts'
17	import { eventsUrl, type FeedSource } from './feed.ts'
18	
19	/** Connection state the status bar reports. */
20	export type StreamState = 'idle' | 'connecting' | 'open' | 'retrying' | 'closed'
21	
22	/** Callbacks a subscription reports through. */
23	export interface StreamHandlers {
24	  onEvent: (event: RunEvent) => void
25	  onState: (state: StreamState) => void
26	}
27	
28	/** Reconnection backoff, in milliseconds, indexed by consecutive failure count. */
29	const BACKOFF_MS = [800, 1_600, 3_200, 6_400, 10_000] as const
30	
31	/** Share of a recording delivered at once, as the history a live stream replays first. */
32	const BACKFILL_SHARE = 0.55
33	
34	/** Delay between the paced frames that follow a recording's backfill. */
35	const PACE_MS = 330
36	
37	/**
38	 * Parse one `data:` frame.
39	 * @param data - The frame's payload.
40	 * @returns The event, or `undefined` when the frame is not a usable event.
41	 */
42	function parseFrame(data: string): RunEvent | undefined {
43	  let value: unknown
44	  try {
45	    value = JSON.parse(data)
46	  } catch {
47	    // A truncated or heartbeat frame is not an error: the stream stays open and
48	    // the next frame carries the next sequence number.
49	    return undefined
50	  }
51	  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return undefined
52	  const event = value as Partial<RunEvent>
53	  if (
54	    typeof event.seq !== 'number'
55	    || typeof event.sessionId !== 'string'
56	    || typeof event.kind !== 'string'
57	    || typeof event.agentId !== 'string'
58	  ) {
59	    return undefined
60	  }
61	  return event as RunEvent
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * The deduplication key of one frame.
66	 * @param event - A parsed frame.
67	 * @returns Its session and sequence number, which together name it once per run.
68	 */
69	function frameKey(event: RunEvent): string {
70	  return `${event.sessionId}\u0000${String(event.seq)}`
71	}
72	
73	/**
74	 * Subscribe to one run's events until the returned disposer is called.
75	 * @param source - Source from `resolveFeed`; it decides between the live
76	 * stream and a paced recording.
77	 * @param runId - The run to follow.
78	 * @param handlers - Event and state callbacks.
79	 * @returns A disposer that closes the stream and stops any pending retry or
80	 * paced frame.
81	 */
82	export function subscribeRun(source: FeedSource, runId: string, handlers: StreamHandlers): () => void {
83	  const url = eventsUrl(source, runId)
84	  return source.mode === 'live' ? subscribeLive(url, handlers) : subscribeRecorded(url, handlers)
85	}
86	
87	/**
88	 * Follow the feed's Server-Sent Events stream.
89	 *
90	 * The subscription owns its own `EventSource`: `EventSource` reconnects on its
91	 * own after a network drop, and this wrapper additionally reopens after an
92	 * error that closed the source for good, with bounded backoff.
93	 * @param url - The stream's URL.
94	 * @param handlers - Event and state callbacks.
95	 * @returns A disposer that closes the stream and stops any pending retry.
96	 */
97	function subscribeLive(url: string, handlers: StreamHandlers): () => void {
98	  const seen = new Set<string>()
99	  let source: EventSource | undefined
100	  let retry: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
101	  let failures = 0
102	  let disposed = false
103	
104	  const open = (): void => {
105	    if (disposed) return
106	    handlers.onState(failures === 0 ? 'connecting' : 'retrying')
107	    const next = new EventSource(url)
108	    source = next
109	
110	    next.onopen = () => {
111	      failures = 0
112	      handlers.onState('open')
113	    }
114	
115	    next.onmessage = (message: MessageEvent<string>) => {
116	      const event = parseFrame(message.data)
117	      if (event === undefined) return
118	      const key = frameKey(event)
119	      if (seen.has(key)) return
120	      seen.add(key)
121	      handlers.onEvent(event)
122	    }
123	
124	    next.onerror = () => {
125	      // EventSource retries a dropped connection itself and only reports
126	      // CLOSED when it has given up; anything else is a transient reconnect.
127	      if (next.readyState !== EventSource.CLOSED) {
128	        handlers.onState('retrying')
129	        return
130	      }
131	      next.close()
132	      if (disposed) return
133	      const wait = BACKOFF_MS[Math.min(failures, BACKOFF_MS.length - 1)] ?? 10_000
134	      failures += 1
135	      handlers.onState('retrying')
136	      retry = setTimeout(open, wait)
137	    }
138	  }
139	
140	  open()
141	
142	  return () => {
143	    disposed = true
144	    if (retry !== undefined) clearTimeout(retry)
145	    source?.close()
146	    handlers.onState('closed')
147	  }
148	}
149	
150	/**
151	 * Replay one committed recording the way the feed streams a run: the first
152	 * BACKFILL_SHARE of its frames at once, as the history a live stream replays on
153	 * connect, then one frame every PACE_MS, then silence with the subscription
154	 * open. A keyless demo therefore shows an enterprise at work rather than a
155	 * static file.
156	 * @param url - The JSON Lines recording's URL.
157	 * @param handlers - Event and state callbacks.
158	 * @returns A disposer that stops the paced frames.
159	 */
160	function subscribeRecorded(url: string, handlers: StreamHandlers): () => void {
161	  let disposed = false
162	  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
163	  handlers.onState('connecting')
164	  void fetch(url, { cache: 'no-store' })
165	    .then(async (response) => {
166	      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`${url} answered ${response.status}`)
167	      return await response.text()
168	    })
169	    .then((text) => {
170	      if (disposed) return
171	      const events = text.split('\n').map(parseFrame).filter((event): event is RunEvent => event !== undefined)
172	      handlers.onState('open')
173	      const backfill = Math.floor(events.length * BACKFILL_SHARE)
174	      for (const event of events.slice(0, backfill)) handlers.onEvent(event)
175	      let cursor = backfill
176	      const tick = (): void => {
177	        const event = events[cursor]
178	        if (disposed || event === undefined) return
179	        handlers.onEvent(event)
180	        cursor += 1
181	        timer = setTimeout(tick, PACE_MS)
182	      }
183	      timer = setTimeout(tick, PACE_MS)
184	    })
185	    .catch(() => {
186	      // A recording that cannot be read leaves the run without events: the
187	      // status bar shows the closed stream and the views keep the roster.
188	      if (!disposed) handlers.onState('closed')
189	    })
190	  return () => {
191	    disposed = true
192	    if (timer !== undefined) clearTimeout(timer)
193	    handlers.onState('closed')
194	  }
195	}
196

1	/**
2	 * The program pipeline the process view draws.
3	 *
4	 * Four stages, left to right, are fixed: work is produced in departments,
5	 * executed against checks by Verification, scored by Judging, and merged by
6	 * Integration. Which lanes exist in the first stage is read from the run
7	 * itself, so a code-safety run shows its six safety departments and a program
8	 * run shows its four department goals.
9	 *
10	 * The scene metrics live here as well, because the gates, the lane rails, the
11	 * floor grid, the time plane and the camera must all agree on one coordinate
12	 * system: the pipeline runs along +x, the lanes are spread along z, and the
13	 * gates stand vertically in y.
14	 */
15	
16	import type { Agent, RunEvent } from './contract.ts'
17	import { departmentColor, divisionColor, EDGE_COLOR } from './palette.ts'
18	
19	/** One stage of the pipeline. */
20	export interface Stage {
21	  id: string
22	  name: string
23	  /** Scene x of the stage's gate; for `departments`, of the lane origin. */
24	  x: number
25	  /** Hex colour of the gate's edges, floor pool and arrivals. */
26	  color: string
27	}
28	
29	/**
30	 * The four stages, in order.
31	 *
32	 * The three gates take the colour of the roster edge kind that names what they
33	 * do — `verifies`, `judges`, `merges` — so a gate and the relationship it
34	 * stands for read as one colour across the deck. Departments have no gate; the
35	 * neutral is the lane origin's own glow, behind the per-lane rail colours.
36	 */
37	export const STAGES: readonly Stage[] = [
38	  { id: 'departments', name: 'Departments', x: -78, color: '#6d80a8' },
39	  { id: 'verification', name: 'Verification', x: -26, color: EDGE_COLOR.verifies },
40	  { id: 'judging', name: 'Judging', x: 14, color: EDGE_COLOR.judges },
41	  { id: 'integration', name: 'Integration', x: 54, color: EDGE_COLOR.merges },
42	]
43	
44	/** Scene metrics every part of the process view measures against. */
45	export const PIPELINE = {
46	  /** x where the lane rails begin, left of the lane origin. */
47	  railStart: -106,
48	  /** x where the lane rails end, right of the Integration gate. */
49	  railEnd: 74,
50	  /** Distance between two neighbouring lane rails. */
51	  laneSpan: 16,
52	  /** y of the lane rails; the comets ride just above them. */
53	  railY: 0,
54	  /** y of the floor grid the gates stand on. */
55	  floorY: -12,
56	  /** y of a gate's top beam. */
57	  gateTop: 30,
58	  /** How far a gate reaches in z beyond the outermost lane. */
59	  gateMargin: 7,
60	} as const
61	
62	/**
63	 * Which stage one event belongs to.
64	 * @param event - The event to place.
65	 * @param agent - The acting agent, when the roster knows it.
66	 * @returns The stage index, `0` when the event is departmental work.
67	 */
68	export function stageOf(event: RunEvent, agent: Agent | undefined): number {
69	  if (event.kind === 'merge') return 3
70	  const division = agent?.division ?? event.agentId.split('/')[0] ?? ''
71	  if (division === 'verification') return 1
72	  if (division === 'judging') return 2
73	  if (division === 'governance') return 3
74	  if (division === 'curation') return 3
75	  if (event.agentId.includes('integration') || event.agentId.includes('release')) return 3
76	  return 0
77	}
78	
79	/**
80	 * Which first-stage lane one event belongs to.
81	 * @param event - The event to place.
82	 * @param agent - The acting agent, when the roster knows it.
83	 * @returns The lane key: a department where the agent has one, else its division.
84	 */
85	function laneOf(event: RunEvent, agent: Agent | undefined): string {
86	  if (agent?.department !== undefined) return agent.department
87	  if (agent !== undefined) return agent.division
88	  return event.agentId.split('/')[0] ?? 'unknown'
89	}
90	
91	/** One department lane of the first stage. */
92	interface Lane {
93	  key: string
94	  /** Roster name of the agent that emitted most of the lane's events. */
95	  label: string
96	  /** The lane's rail colour. */
97	  color: string
98	  /** Every agent seen on the lane, which is what the activity clock is read for. */
99	  agentIds: readonly string[]
100	}
101	
102	/** Lanes discovered in a run, in first-appearance order. */
103	export interface Lanes {
104	  list: readonly Lane[]
105	  /** Lane key to its position in `list`. */
106	  index: ReadonlyMap<string, number>
107	}
108	
109	/** How many first-stage lanes the pipeline draws before it stops adding. */
110	const MAX_LANES = 8
111	
112	/**
113	 * How many events lane discovery reads.
114	 *
115	 * Lanes, their members and their busiest agent settle in the opening minute of
116	 * a run, so the scan stops well inside the event window and the lane set stops
117	 * moving underneath the scene while the rest of the run streams in.
118	 */
119	const LANE_SCAN = 1_000
120	
121	/** Total hue spread, in degrees, given to lanes that share one division colour. */
122	const LANE_HUE_BAND = 84
123	
124	/**
125	 * Split one hex colour into its unit red, green and blue channels.
126	 * @param hex - A `#rrggbb` colour.
127	 * @returns The three channels, each in `0..1`.
128	 */
129	function channels(hex: string): [number, number, number] {
130	  const value = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(1), 16)
131	  return [((value >> 16) & 255) / 255, ((value >> 8) & 255) / 255, (value & 255) / 255]
132	}
133	
134	/**
135	 * One channel of an HSL colour back in RGB.
136	 * @param p - The lower bound the hue interpolates from.
137	 * @param q - The upper bound the hue interpolates to.
138	 * @param t - Hue position, wrapped into `0..1`.
139	 * @returns The channel value in `0..1`.
140	 */
141	function hueChannel(p: number, q: number, t: number): number {
142	  const wrapped = (t + 1) % 1
143	  if (wrapped < 1 / 6) return p + ((q - p) * 6 * wrapped)
144	  if (wrapped < 1 / 2) return q
145	  if (wrapped < 2 / 3) return p + ((q - p) * ((2 / 3) - wrapped) * 6)
146	  return p
147	}
148	
149	/**
150	 * Rotate one colour around the hue circle, keeping its saturation and lightness.
151	 * @param hex - A `#rrggbb` colour.
152	 * @param degrees - Hue offset, in degrees.
153	 * @returns The rotated colour as `#rrggbb`.
154	 */
155	function shiftHue(hex: string, degrees: number): string {
156	  if (degrees === 0) return hex
157	  const [red, green, blue] = channels(hex)
158	  const max = Math.max(red, green, blue)
159	  const min = Math.min(red, green, blue)
160	  const lightness = (max + min) / 2
161	  if (max === min) return hex
162	  const delta = max - min
163	  const saturation = lightness > 0.5 ? delta / (2 - max - min) : delta / (max + min)
164	  const base = max === red
165	    ? ((green - blue) / delta) + (green < blue ? 6 : 0)
166	    : max === green ? ((blue - red) / delta) + 2 : ((red - green) / delta) + 4
167	  const hue = (base / 6) + (degrees / 360)
168	  const q = lightness < 0.5 ? lightness * (1 + saturation) : lightness + saturation - (lightness * saturation)
169	  const p = (2 * lightness) - q
170	  const byte = (value: number): string => Math.round(Math.min(1, Math.max(0, value)) * 255).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')
171	  return `#${byte(hueChannel(p, q, hue + (1 / 3)))}${byte(hueChannel(p, q, hue))}${byte(hueChannel(p, q, hue - (1 / 3)))}`
172	}
173	
174	/**
175	 * Title-case one lane key, used when the roster does not name the lane's agent.
176	 * @param key - The lane key, such as `dependencies` or `code-safety`.
177	 * @returns The key with each word capitalised.
178	 */
179	function titled(key: string): string {
180	  return key.replace(
181	    /(^|-)([a-z])/g,
182	    (_, lead: string, letter: string) => `${lead === '-' ? ' ' : ''}${letter.toUpperCase()}`,
183	  )
184	}
185	
186	/** A lane under construction while the discovery scan runs. */
187	interface LaneDraft {
188	  key: string
189	  division: string
190	  /** Events per agent seen on the lane, in first-appearance order. */
191	  counts: Map<string, number>
192	}
193	
194	/**
195	 * Discover the first-stage lanes of one run.
196	 *
197	 * Every lane takes its division's colour. Divisions that own several lanes
198	 * spread their lanes across a narrow hue band around that colour, so the
199	 * division stays recognisable while its lanes stay apart; a code-safety
200	 * department takes its fixed {@link departmentColor} instead, so it is the
201	 * same colour here as on the code city whatever order the departments start in.
202	 * @param events - The run's event window, oldest first.
203	 * @param agents - The roster index.
204	 * @returns The lanes in first-appearance order.
205	 */
206	export function discoverLanes(events: readonly RunEvent[], agents: Map<string, Agent>): Lanes {
207	  const drafts = new Map<string, LaneDraft>()
208	  const order: string[] = []
209	
210	  for (const event of events.slice(0, LANE_SCAN)) {
211	    const agent = agents.get(event.agentId)
212	    if (stageOf(event, agent) !== 0) continue
213	    const key = laneOf(event, agent)
214	    let draft = drafts.get(key)
215	    if (draft === undefined) {
216	      if (order.length >= MAX_LANES) continue
217	      draft = { key, division: agent?.division ?? key, counts: new Map() }
218	      drafts.set(key, draft)
219	      order.push(key)
220	    }
221	    draft.counts.set(event.agentId, (draft.counts.get(event.agentId) ?? 0) + 1)
222	  }
223	
224	  const shared = new Map<string, string[]>()
225	  for (const key of order) {
226	    const base = divisionColor(drafts.get(key)?.division ?? key)
227	    const group = shared.get(base) ?? []
228	    group.push(key)
229	    shared.set(base, group)
230	  }
231	  const colors = new Map<string, string>()
232	  for (const [base, group] of shared) {
233	    for (const [position, key] of group.entries()) {
234	      const spread = group.length < 2 ? 0 : ((position / (group.length - 1)) - 0.5) * LANE_HUE_BAND
235	      colors.set(key, departmentColor(key) ?? shiftHue(base, spread))
236	    }
237	  }
238	
239	  const list = order.map((key) => {
240	    const draft = drafts.get(key)
241	    const agentIds = [...(draft?.counts.keys() ?? [])]
242	    let principal = agentIds[0]
243	    let best = 0
244	    for (const [agentId, total] of draft?.counts ?? []) {
245	      if (total <= best) continue
246	      best = total
247	      principal = agentId
248	    }
249	    return {
250	      key,
251	      label: (principal === undefined ? undefined : agents.get(principal)?.name) ?? titled(key),
252	      color: colors.get(key) ?? divisionColor(key),
253	      agentIds,
254	    }
255	  })
256	
257	  return { list, index: new Map(list.map((lane, position) => [lane.key, position])) }
258	}
259	
260	/**
261	 * Scene z of one lane.
262	 * @param index - Lane position in `Lanes.list`.
263	 * @param total - How many lanes the pipeline holds.
264	 * @returns The lane's z, centred on the pipeline axis; the first lane is the
265	 * farthest from the camera, so the lanes read top to bottom as the panel lists them.
266	 */
267	export function laneZ(index: number, total: number): number {
268	  return (index - ((total - 1) / 2)) * PIPELINE.laneSpan
269	}
270	
271	/**
272	 * Half the width in z that a gate, the floor pool and the time plane span.
273	 * @param total - How many lanes the pipeline holds.
274	 * @returns The half-width, always wide enough to clear the outermost lane.
275	 */
276	export function pipelineHalfWidth(total: number): number {
277	  return (Math.max(total - 1, 1) * PIPELINE.laneSpan / 2) + PIPELINE.gateMargin
278	}
279	
280	/** Where one event travels, in stage terms. */
281	export interface Flight {
282	  /** The stage the event was logged at. */
283	  stage: number
284	  /** Lane position for departmental work, `-1` for anything later in the pipeline. */
285	  lane: number
286	  /** Scene x the comet leaves from. */
287	  fromX: number
288	  /** Scene x of the gate the comet arrives at. */
289	  toX: number
290	  /** The stage whose gate the comet arrives at. */
291	  arrival: number
292	}
293	
294	/**
295	 * The flight one event's comet takes.
296	 *
297	 * Work travels to the next gate. An event logged at Integration has no next
298	 * gate, so it is drawn arriving at Integration from Judging: a merge is only
299	 * ever seen landing.
300	 * @param event - The event to place.
301	 * @param agent - The acting agent, when the roster knows it.
302	 * @param lanes - The discovered lanes, which place departmental work.
303	 * @returns The flight's stages and its two x positions.
304	 */
305	export function flightOf(event: RunEvent, agent: Agent | undefined, lanes: Lanes): Flight {
306	  const stage = stageOf(event, agent)
307	  const last = STAGES.length - 1
308	  const arrival = Math.min(stage + 1, last)
309	  const source = stage === last ? last - 1 : stage
310	  return {
311	    stage,
312	    lane: stage === 0 ? lanes.index.get(laneOf(event, agent)) ?? -1 : -1,
313	    fromX: STAGES[source]?.x ?? 0,
314	    toX: STAGES[arrival]?.x ?? 0,
315	    arrival,
316	  }
317	}
318	
319	/**
320	 * How many events each lane has produced.
321	 * @param events - The events the timeline admits.
322	 * @param agents - The roster index.
323	 * @param lanes - The discovered lanes.
324	 * @returns One total per lane, indexed as `Lanes.list`.
325	 */
326	export function laneTotals(
327	  events: readonly RunEvent[],
328	  agents: Map<string, Agent>,
329	  lanes: Lanes,
330	): number[] {
331	  const totals = lanes.list.map(() => 0)
332	  for (const event of events) {
333	    const agent = agents.get(event.agentId)
334	    if (stageOf(event, agent) !== 0) continue
335	    const position = lanes.index.get(laneOf(event, agent))
336	    if (position === undefined) continue
337	    totals[position] = (totals[position] ?? 0) + 1
338	  }
339	  return totals
340	}

1	/**
2	 * The followed run's own workflow graph, derived from its event stream.
3	 *
4	 * A node is one session of the run, named by the seat that acted in it. The
5	 * relationships between sessions are not carried by any frame: the feed folds
6	 * a program run's sessions under one id — the root is `program-<digest>`, a
7	 * department is `program-<digest>-<department>` and the integration session is
8	 * the `@integration` child, which the feed decodes from the `~0040` escape the
9	 * session directory is written with. This module reads that naming and nothing
10	 * else, so a run whose sessions are not named that way — a fleet or an
11	 * experiment, whose cells are `environment-<uuid>` — falls back to the pipeline
12	 * stage each session's work was logged at, and draws no spawn edges, because
13	 * nothing in the run states who started whom.
14	 *
15	 * Everything here is a pure function of the events the timeline admits, so
16	 * scrubbing or replaying the timeline rebuilds the graph as it stood then.
17	 */
18	
19	import type { Agent, RunEvent } from './contract.ts'
20	import { divisionColor } from './palette.ts'
21	import { discoverLanes, stageOf } from './pipeline.ts'
22	import { eventTimeMs } from './store.ts'
23	
24	/**
25	 * A program run's session ids: the kind, the program's content digest, and the
26	 * department or `@integration` suffix of a child.
27	 */
28	const PROGRAM_SESSION = /^(program-[0-9a-f]{8,})(?:-.+)?$/
29	
30	/** The integration suffix, after the `@` or its `~0040` escape is stripped. */
31	const INTEGRATION = 'integration'
32	
33	/** Distance between two tiers, along +x. */
34	const TIER_SPAN = 76
35	
36	/** Distance between two nodes of one tier, along y, where the tier has room. */
37	const NODE_SPAN = 32
38	
39	/**
40	 * How much room in y one tier is given.
41	 *
42	 * A tier packs its nodes closer rather than growing past this, because a fleet
43	 * run opens dozens of cells at once and a graph the camera cannot frame shows
44	 * nothing at all.
45	 */
46	const TIER_HEIGHT = 300
47	
48	/** Spacing below which a node's name would sit on its neighbour's. */
49	const NAME_SPACING = 18
50	
51	/** Clear space kept around the graph when the camera frames it. */
52	const MARGIN = 22
53	
54	/** Colour of a node the roster places in no division. */
55	const NEUTRAL = '#8296b8'
56	
57	/** One session of the run. */
58	export interface WorkflowNode {
59	  /** The session id, which is the node's identity across rebuilds. */
60	  id: string
61	  /** Roster name of the seat that acted most in the session, else its agent id. */
62	  label: string
63	  /** The seat that acted most in the session; `undefined` for an implied node. */
64	  agentId: string | undefined
65	  tier: number
66	  x: number
67	  y: number
68	  color: string
69	  /** How many admitted frames the session logged. */
70	  events: number
71	  certificates: number
72	  merges: number
73	  refusals: number
74	  directives: number
75	  /** Whether the session's work is the run's integration step. */
76	  integration: boolean
77	  /** When the session's newest admitted frame was logged, or `NaN` with none. */
78	  lastMs: number
79	  /** The newest admitted frame's label, or `undefined` with none. */
80	  lastLabel: string | undefined
81	  /**
82	   * Whether the session is named only by its children's ids.
83	   *
84	   * A run's root emits little and late, so a cut of the timeline that has not
85	   * reached its first frame still has to draw the parent its children hang off.
86	   */
87	  implied: boolean
88	}
89	
90	/** A directed relationship the graph draws between two sessions. */
91	interface WorkflowEdge {
92	  id: string
93	  from: string
94	  to: string
95	  /** `spawn` is the naming relationship; `merge` is a certified result joining integration. */
96	  kind: 'spawn' | 'merge'
97	  /**
98	   * Whether the parent logged the delegation itself.
99	   *
100	   * A logged `delegation` names the relationship at the moment it is made, so
101	   * its edge is drawn at once instead of growing as the child's first frame
102	   * arrives.
103	   */
104	  immediate: boolean
105	}
106	
107	/** The graph one cut of the timeline produces. */
108	export interface WorkflowGraph {
109	  nodes: readonly WorkflowNode[]
110	  edges: readonly WorkflowEdge[]
111	  byId: ReadonlyMap<string, WorkflowNode>
112	  /** How many admitted frames carry a certificate, across every session. */
113	  certificates: number
114	  /** How many admitted frames carry a merge, across every session. */
115	  merges: number
116	  /** The largest event count on any node; the node meters are read against it. */
117	  busiest: number
118	  /**
119	   * Whether a tier had to pack its nodes closer than a name needs.
120	   *
121	   * The scene drops the names at that point and leaves the sessions to the
122	   * hover card and the panel, rather than printing them over each other.
123	   */
124	  dense: boolean
125	  /** Half the graph's reach in x and y, which is what the camera frames. */
126	  extent: { x: number; y: number }
127	}
128	
129	/** One session under construction while the scan runs. */
130	interface Draft {

130	interface Draft {
131	  id: string
132	  /** Frames per acting agent, in first-appearance order. */
133	  counts: Map<string, number>
134	  events: number
135	  certificates: number
136	  merges: number
137	  refusals: number
138	  directives: number
139	  lastMs: number
140	  lastLabel: string | undefined
141	  /** The lowest pipeline stage the session's work was logged at. */
142	  stage: number
143	}
144	
145	/**
146	 * The integration suffix in any of the forms a session directory carries it.
147	 * @param suffix - The session id's suffix under the run root.
148	 * @returns Whether the suffix names the integration session.
149	 */
150	function isIntegration(suffix: string): boolean {
151	  return suffix.replace(/^(@|~0040)/, '') === INTEGRATION
152	}
153	
154	/**
155	 * What one session id carries under the run root.
156	 * @param id - The session id.
157	 * @param root - The run root, when the ids state one.
158	 * @returns The suffix, empty for the root itself and for a run with no root.
159	 */
160	function suffixOf(id: string, root: string | undefined): string {
161	  return root === undefined || id === root ? '' : id.slice(root.length + 1)
162	}
163	
164	/**
165	 * The run root every session hangs off, when the ids state one.
166	 * @param ids - Every session id the admitted events carry.
167	 * @returns The root session id, or `undefined` when the run names no hierarchy.
168	 */
169	function rootOf(ids: readonly string[]): string | undefined {
170	  let root: string | undefined
171	  for (const id of ids) {
172	    const match = PROGRAM_SESSION.exec(id)
173	    if (match === null) return undefined
174	    const candidate = match[1]
175	    if (candidate === undefined) return undefined
176	    if (root === undefined) root = candidate
177	    // Two programs folded into one stream share no root, so neither owns the graph.
178	    else if (root !== candidate) return undefined
179	  }
180	  return root
181	}
182	
183	/**
184	 * A short, stable name for a session no admitted frame acts in.
185	 * @param id - The session id.
186	 * @returns The id truncated to its kind and the head of its digest.
187	 */
188	function shortId(id: string): string {
189	  return id.length <= 24 ? id : `${id.slice(0, 22)}…`
190	}
191	
192	/**
193	 * The session one session was started under.
194	 *
195	 * The longest id the child's own id extends is the parent, so a grandchild
196	 * hangs off its own parent rather than off the run root. Matching on the whole
197	 * parent id rather than on the suffix's separators is what keeps a department
198	 * whose name carries a hyphen in the tier its parent puts it in.
199	 * @param id - The child session id.
200	 * @param ids - Every session id the graph holds.
201	 * @returns The parent session id, or `undefined` for a session that extends none.
202	 */
203	function parentOf(id: string, ids: readonly string[]): string | undefined {
204	  let parent: string | undefined
205	  for (const candidate of ids) {
206	    if (candidate === id || !id.startsWith(`${candidate}-`)) continue
207	    if (parent === undefined || candidate.length > parent.length) parent = candidate
208	  }
209	  return parent
210	}
211	
212	/**
213	 * Scan the admitted events into one draft per session.
214	 * @param events - The events the timeline admits, in any order.
215	 * @param agents - The roster index, which places each frame in the pipeline.
216	 * @returns The drafts, in first-appearance order.
217	 */
218	function draftSessions(events: readonly RunEvent[], agents: Map<string, Agent>): Draft[] {
219	  const drafts = new Map<string, Draft>()
220	  for (const event of events) {
221	    let draft = drafts.get(event.sessionId)
222	    if (draft === undefined) {
223	      draft = {
224	        id: event.sessionId,
225	        counts: new Map(),
226	        events: 0,
227	        certificates: 0,
228	        merges: 0,
229	        refusals: 0,
230	        directives: 0,
231	        lastMs: Number.NaN,
232	        lastLabel: undefined,
233	        stage: stageOf(event, agents.get(event.agentId)),
234	      }
235	      drafts.set(event.sessionId, draft)
236	    }
237	    draft.events += 1
238	    draft.counts.set(event.agentId, (draft.counts.get(event.agentId) ?? 0) + 1)
239	    if (event.kind === 'certificate') draft.certificates += 1
240	    if (event.kind === 'merge') draft.merges += 1
241	    if (event.kind === 'refusal') draft.refusals += 1
242	    if (event.kind === 'directive') draft.directives += 1
243	    draft.stage = Math.min(draft.stage, stageOf(event, agents.get(event.agentId)))
244	    const at = eventTimeMs(event)
245	    if (Number.isNaN(draft.lastMs) || (!Number.isNaN(at) && at >= draft.lastMs)) {
246	      draft.lastMs = at
247	      draft.lastLabel = event.label
248	    }
249	  }
250	  return [...drafts.values()]
251	}
252	
253	/**
254	 * The seat that did most of one session's work.
255	 * @param counts - Frames per acting agent.
256	 * @returns The agent id, or `undefined` when the session logged nothing.
257	 */
258	function principalOf(counts: ReadonlyMap<string, number>): string | undefined {
259	  let principal: string | undefined
260	  let best = 0
261	  for (const [agentId, total] of counts) {
262	    if (total <= best) continue
263	    best = total
264	    principal = agentId
265	  }
266	  return principal
267	}
268	
269	/**
270	 * Lane colour per acting agent, so a department reads in the same colour here
271	 * as on its rail in the process view.
272	 * @param events - The events the timeline admits.
273	 * @param agents - The roster index.
274	 * @returns One colour per agent id the lanes cover.
275	 */
276	function laneColors(events: readonly RunEvent[], agents: Map<string, Agent>): Map<string, string> {
277	  const colors = new Map<string, string>()
278	  for (const lane of discoverLanes(events, agents).list) {
279	    for (const agentId of lane.agentIds) colors.set(agentId, lane.color)
280	  }
281	  return colors
282	}
283	
284	/**
285	 * Tier each session sits in, left to right.
286	 *
287	 * Under a program root the tier is the depth of the id's prefix chain, and the
288	 * integration session is pushed past the deepest department whatever its own
289	 * depth, because integration is the last thing the run does. With no root the
290	 * tier is the pipeline stage the session's earliest work was logged at.
291	 * @param drafts - The scanned sessions.
292	 * @param root - The run root, when the ids state one.
293	 * @param parents - The parent session id per child, where the ids state one.
294	 * @returns The tier per session id.
295	 */
296	function tiersOf(drafts: readonly Draft[], root: string | undefined, parents: ReadonlyMap<string, string>): Map<string, number> {
297	  const tiers = new Map<string, number>()
298	  if (root === undefined) {
299	    for (const draft of drafts) tiers.set(draft.id, draft.stage)
300	    return tiers
301	  }
302	
303	  const depthOf = (id: string): number => {
304	    let depth = 0
305	    let walk = parents.get(id)
306	    while (walk !== undefined) {
307	      depth += 1
308	      walk = parents.get(walk)
309	    }
310	    return depth
311	  }
312	
313	  const integration: string[] = []
314	  let deepest = 0
315	  for (const draft of drafts) {
316	    if (isIntegration(suffixOf(draft.id, root))) {
317	      integration.push(draft.id)
318	      continue
319	    }
320	    const depth = depthOf(draft.id)
321	    deepest = Math.max(deepest, depth)
322	    tiers.set(draft.id, depth)
323	  }
324	  for (const id of integration) tiers.set(id, deepest + 1)
325	  return tiers
326	}
327	
328	/**
329	 * The workflow graph of one cut of a run.
330	 * @param events - The events the timeline admits, in any order.
331	 * @param agents - The roster index, which names the seat acting in each session.
332	 * @returns The nodes, the edges between them, and what the camera frames.
333	 */
334	export function layoutWorkflow(events: readonly RunEvent[], agents: Map<string, Agent>): WorkflowGraph {
335	  // Frames arrive in the order the feed folds its sessions, not the order they
336	  // were logged, so the scan reads the logged order: a tier then fans its
337	  // sessions out in the order they first reported, and a department takes the
338	  // same lane colour here as it does on its rail in the process view.
339	  const logged = [...events].sort((left, right) => eventTimeMs(left) - eventTimeMs(right))
340	  const drafts = draftSessions(logged, agents)
341	  const root = rootOf(drafts.map(draft => draft.id))
342	  // The root emits its merges last, so a cut short of them still has to draw it.
343	  if (root !== undefined && !drafts.some(draft => draft.id === root)) {
344	    drafts.unshift({
345	      id: root,
346	      counts: new Map(),
347	      events: 0,
348	      certificates: 0,
349	      merges: 0,
350	      refusals: 0,
351	      directives: 0,
352	      lastMs: Number.NaN,
353	      lastLabel: undefined,
354	      stage: 0,
355	    })
356	  }
357	
358	  const ids = drafts.map(draft => draft.id)
359	  const parents = new Map<string, string>()
360	  for (const id of ids) {
361	    const parent = parentOf(id, ids)
362	    if (parent !== undefined) parents.set(id, parent)
363	  }
364	
365	  const tiers = tiersOf(drafts, root, parents)
366	  const colors = laneColors(logged, agents)
367	  const perTier = new Map<number, Draft[]>()
368	  for (const draft of drafts) {
369	    const tier = tiers.get(draft.id) ?? 0
370	    const row = perTier.get(tier) ?? []
371	    row.push(draft)
372	    perTier.set(tier, row)
373	  }
374	  const spread = [...perTier.keys()].sort((left, right) => left - right)
375	
376	  const nodes: WorkflowNode[] = []
377	  let dense = false
378	  for (const [column, tier] of spread.entries()) {
379	    const row = perTier.get(tier) ?? []
380	    const span = Math.min(NODE_SPAN, TIER_HEIGHT / Math.max(1, row.length - 1))
381	    dense = dense || (row.length > 1 && span < NAME_SPACING)
382	    for (const [index, draft] of row.entries()) {
383	      const principal = principalOf(draft.counts)
384	      const agent = principal === undefined ? undefined : agents.get(principal)
385	      nodes.push({
386	        id: draft.id,
387	        label: agent?.name ?? principal ?? shortId(draft.id),
388	        agentId: principal,
389	        tier: column,
390	        x: (column - ((spread.length - 1) / 2)) * TIER_SPAN,
391	        y: (((row.length - 1) / 2) - index) * span,
392	        color: (principal === undefined ? undefined : colors.get(principal))
393	          ?? (agent === undefined ? NEUTRAL : divisionColor(agent.division)),
394	        events: draft.events,
395	        certificates: draft.certificates,
396	        merges: draft.merges,
397	        refusals: draft.refusals,
398	        directives: draft.directives,
399	        integration: isIntegration(suffixOf(draft.id, root)),
400	        lastMs: draft.lastMs,
401	        lastLabel: draft.lastLabel,
402	        implied: draft.events === 0,
403	      })
404	    }
405	  }
406	
407	  const byId = new Map(nodes.map(node => [node.id, node]))
408	  const delegating = new Set(
409	    logged.filter(event => event.kind === 'delegation').map(event => event.sessionId),
410	  )
411	  const edges: WorkflowEdge[] = []
412	  for (const node of nodes) {
413	    const parent = parents.get(node.id)
414	    if (parent === undefined) continue
415	    edges.push({
416	      id: `spawn:${node.id}`,
417	      from: parent,
418	      to: node.id,
419	      kind: 'spawn',
420	      immediate: delegating.has(parent),
421	    })
422	  }
423	
424	  const merges = nodes.reduce((total, node) => total + node.merges, 0)
425	  const integration = nodes.find(node => node.integration)
426	  if (merges > 0 && integration !== undefined) {
427	    for (const node of nodes) {
428	      if (node.integration || node.id === root || node.certificates === 0) continue
429	      edges.push({ id: `merge:${node.id}`, from: node.id, to: integration.id, kind: 'merge', immediate: false })
430	    }
431	  }
432	
433	  return {
434	    nodes,
435	    edges,
436	    byId,
437	    certificates: nodes.reduce((total, node) => total + node.certificates, 0),
438	    merges,
439	    busiest: nodes.reduce((most, node) => Math.max(most, node.events), 0),
440	    dense,
441	    extent: {
442	      x: nodes.reduce((reach, node) => Math.max(reach, Math.abs(node.x)), 0) + MARGIN,
443	      y: nodes.reduce((reach, node) => Math.max(reach, Math.abs(node.y)), 0) + MARGIN,
444	    },
445	  }
446	}

1	/**
2	 * The deck's single client store.
3	 *
4	 * Two kinds of state live here. React state (roster, runs, events, selection)
5	 * drives rendering. Frame state — `activity`, `bursts` and `openingFrame` — is
6	 * mutated in place and read from `useFrame`, because a sixty-times-a-second
7	 * render pass must not go through React at all.
8	 */
9	
10	'use client'
11	
12	import { create } from 'zustand'
13	import type { Roster, Run, RunEvent, SafetyReview } from './contract.ts'
14	import { getRoster, getRuns, getSafety, resolveFeed, type FeedSource } from './feed.ts'
15	import { subscribeRun, type StreamState } from './stream.ts'
16	
17	/** How many events one run keeps in memory; older frames fall off the head. */
18	const EVENT_WINDOW = 4_000
19	
20	/** How often a live deck re-reads the run list and a running review's detail. */
21	const REFRESH_MS = 10_000
22	
23	/** A certificate burst waiting to be drawn once, then dropped. */
24	interface Burst {
25	  agentId: string
26	  at: number
27	}
28	
29	/**
30	 * How the deck is being shown.
31	 *
32	 * `off` is the working deck: header, stage and panel. `focus` hides the panel
33	 * and gives the stage the whole frame. `tour` is `focus` plus a timer that
34	 * walks the three views, announcing each one; anything the viewer does ends it.
35	 */
36	type PresentationMode = 'off' | 'focus' | 'tour'
37	
38	/**
39	 * How far the cold open has got.
40	 *
41	 * It runs at most once per page load: `idle` is a deck that has not opened,
42	 * `playing` the sequence itself, and `done` a deck that has already assembled,
43	 * which is why a second tour starts on its first view instead of replaying it.
44	 */
45	type OpeningPhase = 'idle' | 'playing' | 'done'
46	
47	/**
48	 * Frame state the cold open drives.
49	 *
50	 * `reveal` walks from 0, with the graph dark, to 1, with every division lit.
51	 * The enterprise layers read it from `useFrame` and turn it into per-division
52	 * progress; nothing renders on it, so the sequence costs no React work.
53	 */
54	interface OpeningFrame {
55	  reveal: number
56	}
57	
58	/**
59	 * The grade the shared stage renders at.
60	 *
61	 * The three tiers trade image for frame time: pixel ratio, the antialiasing
62	 * pass and the bloom are what a weak GPU cannot afford.
63	 */
64	export type QualityTier = 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'
65	
66	/** Everything the deck holds for one session. */
67	export interface DeckState {
68	  source: FeedSource | undefined
69	  streamState: StreamState
70	  roster: Roster | undefined
71	  runs: Run[]
72	  selectedRunId: string | undefined
73	  events: RunEvent[]
74	  safety: SafetyReview | undefined
75	  safetyRunId: string | undefined
76	  selectedAgentId: string | undefined
77	  selectedFindingId: string | undefined
78	  error: string | undefined
79	  booted: boolean
80	  /** Timeline position as an epoch-millisecond cap; `undefined` follows the head. */
81	  cursor: number | undefined
82	  /** Last activity timestamp per agent, in `performance.now()` milliseconds. */
83	  activity: Map<string, number>
84	  /** Certificate bursts the enterprise scene has not drawn yet. */
85	  bursts: Burst[]
86	  /** How the deck is being shown; presentation only, no effect on what is read. */
87	  presentation: PresentationMode
88	  /** How far the cold open has got; it runs at most once per page load. */
89	  opening: OpeningPhase
90	  /** `performance.now()` at which the running sequence started, or `undefined` outside one. */
91	  openingAt: number | undefined
92	  /** The cold open's frame state, mutated in place and read from `useFrame`. */
93	  openingFrame: OpeningFrame
94	  /** The grade the stage renders at, kept across a view change so a learned tier is not relearned. */
95	  qualityTier: QualityTier
96	  /** Whether a `?quality=` query pinned the tier, which also stops the performance monitor. */
97	  qualityPinned: boolean
98	  boot: () => Promise<void>
99	  selectRun: (id: string) => void
100	  /** List a run the feed does not report yet, such as a review this deck just started. */
101	  addRun: (run: Run) => void
102	  /** Re-read the run list and, while the followed review is still running, its detail. */
103	  refresh: () => Promise<void>
104	  selectAgent: (id: string | undefined) => void
105	  selectFinding: (id: string | undefined) => void
106	  setCursor: (atMs: number | undefined) => void
107	  /** Load a review's detail; `force` re-reads one already loaded. */
108	  loadSafety: (id: string, force?: boolean) => Promise<void>
109	  setPresentation: (mode: PresentationMode) => void
110	  /** Enter one presentation mode, or leave it when it is already the current one. */
111	  togglePresentation: (mode: Exclude<PresentationMode, 'off'>) => void
112	  /**
113	   * Start the cold open, unless it has already run.
114	   * @param ignite - Whether the graph assembles; `false` holds it at rest, for reduced motion.
115	   * @returns Whether this call started the sequence.
116	   */
117	  startOpening: (ignite: boolean) => boolean
118	  /** End the sequence at once, leaving the graph whole rather than half lit. */
119	  endOpening: () => void
120	  setQualityTier: (tier: QualityTier) => void
121	  /** Fix the tier a `?quality=` query named, which the performance monitor then never moves. */
122	  pinQualityTier: (tier: QualityTier) => void
123	}
124	
125	let unsubscribe: (() => void) | undefined
126	
127	/**
128	 * Append one event to the window, dropping the oldest frames past the cap.
129	 * @param events - The current window.
130	 * @param event - The frame to append.
131	 * @returns The new window.
132	 */
133	function appendEvent(events: RunEvent[], event: RunEvent): RunEvent[] {
134	  const next = [...events, event]
135	  return next.length > EVENT_WINDOW ? next.slice(next.length - EVENT_WINDOW) : next
136	}
137	
138	export const useDeck = create<DeckState>((set, get) => ({
139	  source: undefined,
140	  streamState: 'idle',
141	  roster: undefined,
142	  runs: [],
143	  selectedRunId: undefined,
144	  events: [],
145	  safety: undefined,
146	  safetyRunId: undefined,
147	  selectedAgentId: undefined,
148	  selectedFindingId: undefined,
149	  error: undefined,
150	  booted: false,
151	  cursor: undefined,
152	  activity: new Map<string, number>(),
153	  bursts: [],
154	  presentation: 'off',
155	  opening: 'idle',
156	  openingAt: undefined,
157	  openingFrame: { reveal: 1 },
158	  qualityTier: 'high',
159	  qualityPinned: false,
160	
161	  boot: async () => {
162	    if (get().booted) return
163	    set({ booted: true })
164	    const source = await resolveFeed()
165	    set({ source })
166	    try {
167	      const [roster, runs] = await Promise.all([getRoster(source), getRuns(source)])
168	      set({ roster, runs })
169	      const safetyRun = runs.find(run => run.kind === 'code-safety') ?? runs[0]
170	      if (safetyRun !== undefined) get().selectRun(safetyRun.id)
171	    } catch (error) {
172	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
173	    }
174	    // Replay is a fixed record; only a live feed changes underneath the deck.
175	    if (source.mode === 'live') setInterval(() => { void get().refresh() }, REFRESH_MS)
176	  },
177	
178	  addRun: (run) => {
179	    set(state => (state.runs.some(entry => entry.id === run.id) ? {} : { runs: [run, ...state.runs] }))
180	  },
181	
182	  refresh: async () => {
183	    const { source, runs: known, selectedRunId } = get()
184	    if (source === undefined) return
185	    try {
186	      const listed = await getRuns(source)
187	      // A review this deck started stays listed until the feed reports it.
188	      const pending = known.filter(run => !listed.some(entry => entry.id === run.id))
189	      set({ runs: [...pending, ...listed] })
190	      const selected = [...pending, ...listed].find(run => run.id === selectedRunId)
191	      // The refresh that first reports a review as no longer running re-reads it
192	      // once more: the certificate lands after the last read made while it ran,
193	      // and a deck that stopped reading at that moment would never show it.
194	      const wasRunning = known.find(run => run.id === selectedRunId)?.status === 'running'
195	      if (
196	        selected?.kind === 'code-safety'
197	        && (selected.status === 'running' || wasRunning || get().safetyRunId !== selected.id)
198	      ) {
199	        await get().loadSafety(selected.id, true)
200	      }
201	    } catch (error) {
202	      set({ error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) })
203	    }
204	  },
205	
206	  selectRun: (id) => {
207	    const source = get().source
208	    if (source === undefined || get().selectedRunId === id) return
209	    unsubscribe?.()
210	    set({ selectedRunId: id, events: [], cursor: undefined })
211	    const { activity, bursts } = get()
212	    activity.clear()
213	    // A certificate queued under the previous run must not burst on this one.
214	    bursts.length = 0
215	    unsubscribe = subscribeRun(source, id, {
216	      onState: state => set({ streamState: state }),
217	      onEvent: (event) => {
218	        get().activity.set(event.agentId, performance.now())
219	        if (event.kind === 'certificate') {
220	          get().bursts.push({ agentId: event.agentId, at: performance.now() })
221	        }
222	        set(state => ({ events: appendEvent(state.events, event) }))
223	      },
224	    })
225	    const run = get().runs.find(entry => entry.id === id)
226	    if (run?.kind === 'code-safety') void get().loadSafety(id)
227	  },
228	
229	  selectAgent: id => set({ selectedAgentId: id }),
230	  selectFinding: id => set({ selectedFindingId: id }),
231	  setCursor: atMs => set({ cursor: atMs }),
232	
233	  loadSafety: async (id, force = false) => {
234	    const source = get().source
235	    if (source === undefined || (!force && get().safetyRunId === id)) return
